newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen unchanged, Brent 10 cents down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen unchanged, Brent 10 cents down.

text.p: IPE gas oil was called to open little changed on Friday, while Brent was expected to open around 10 cents lower after Thursday's sharp upside move due to disruption to oil production in the Gulf of Mexico by a tropical storm.
September Brent closed 38 cents up at $18.68 a barrel, having peaked at $18.79 two hours before the close. August gas oil ended $3.25 a tonne higher at $167.
"We saw a bit of short-term support but it's only a blip like a very cold snap in the winter," said one broker.
Dealers said that underlying fundamentals were bearish and were likely to prevail.
"I think we'll see a bit of a correction to the move up yesterday, and WTI failed to break some key numbers which made a bit of a softer close" said one.
The September Brent contract came off the highs after front month failed to breach key resistance at $20.24 a barrel.
"Unless there are any further problems in the Gulf coast from this particular storm I can't see prices getting any higher," a dealer said late on Thursday.
Iraq is poised to sell big volumes of oil next month, Germany is to sell oil from stocks and North Sea loadings are not going to be hit hard by oilfield maintenance as previously expected.
